questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The subjects available at Universitat de Barcelona were especially interesting to me. Amongst other subjects, UB offered a course in Economic Growth which focused heavily on the Overlapping Generations Model, which I will be using in my master thesis.

questions.answer: I don't remember. I found the registration process easy, so I did not use any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Classes have a very high workload, and try to choose some courses that do not have so high workload, since it was difficult to manage all the mandatory assignments.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was medium. However, the workload was extremely intense, and it was very difficult to meet all the mandatory deadlines. Moreover, teachers are reluctant to explicitly state the course requirements, which makes it very hard to prioritise time appropriately.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very good teaching, and extremely competent professors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economic Growth II, Cooperative Decisions and Social Choice, Regional and Urban Economics, Empirical Methods in Regional and Urban Economics, Political Economy, Governments and Markets.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Economic Growth II: Heavy workload, but very interesting - especially if you like to work with the overlapping generations model developed by Diamond. 
Cooperative decisions and social choice: Very interesting subject, limited workload during the semester, but heavy assignment at the end of the semester.
